text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy said on Thursday one of its four vote-heavy K-shareholders had approved the sale of shares to British investor, Lord Moyne.
The other three have told the company they would not restart talks on the sale of their K shares, Amer said in a statement.

Amer said the Student Union of the Helsinki School of Economics, "has approved the sales offer of K shares made to Lord Moyne and that the decision became final and binding on the sellers on June 25, 1997."
An Amer spokeswoman earlier said the K shareholders would not reopen talks on the sale of their shares.

The other three -- the Finnish Association of Graduate Engineers, the Finnish Association of Graduates of the Schools of Economics and Business Administration SEFE and the Land and Water Technology Foundation, added they would not start negotiations with any other party, Amer said.

Jonathan Bryan Guinness, the third Lord Moyne, offered early in June to buy almost 60 percent of votes in Amer for 301 million markka. The K-shareholders initially approved the deal but later pulled out.

Amer's four K-shareholders, bound by an agreement to sell or keep their stakes together, have been eager for a long time to divest their holdings. The K-shares control over 90 percent of votes in Amer.
